definition: Models interleaving attention layers with SSM or linear-attention layers (Jamba, Zamba, many 2025-era models) to combine attention's precision with SSMs' efficiency on long contexts.
details: Models interleaving attention layers with SSM or linear-attention layers (Jamba, Zamba, many 2025-era models) to combine attention's precision with SSMs' efficiency on long contexts.

explainer.lead: Hybrid architectures interleave attention layers with SSM or linear-attention layers so a model keeps attention's precision while gaining efficiency on long contexts. They matter because full attention is expensive as context grows.

tiers.eli5: It is like a team where a few specialists check every detail while most workers scan quickly, giving careful handling without paying for it everywhere.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers mix layer types in a stack, often putting attention at a few positions and SSM or linear-attention layers elsewhere; the pitfall is that the ratio and placement of layers strongly affect quality and must be tuned per context length.
tiers.paperLevel: The model is a stack of blocks where some blocks use softmax attention and others use state-space or linear-attention recurrence, e.g. Jamba and Zamba. No universal formula fixes the mix; trade-offs between recall precision and long-context cost are empirical.

explainer.example: A model places attention layers every few blocks and SSM layers between them, letting it process a long document without applying quadratic attention at every layer.
